evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep does not deliver the time-boxed framing or 'quote you can depend on' promise. Jumps directly into the call with 'I was just calling in regards for your request for a move online for October 2nd. Do you have a few moments to go over that?' — no waiting structure or explicit yes-gate.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Soham Sarda), moving day (October 2nd), and destination city (Austin to Austin, 78729) confirmed. Origin address also confirmed (Taylor draper lane, Austin, 78759). Origin square footage asked and provided (650-700 sq ft). Destination address and square footage not explicitly confirmed as a size. Route city-to-city is present but both locations in Austin.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing has begun. Rep states: 'besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call today?' — but this comes after already confirming the phone and email, so it is asked late in the interaction, though before the bulk of logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises pricing concern ('I would like to know more about the pricing'). Rep does not dig deeper with follow-up questions like 'tell me more about that' or 'what specific aspects of pricing concern you?' — instead pivots into Two Promises (damage coverage, on-time guarantee) without exploring the customer's underlying pricing anxiety.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection summary delivered. Customer raises pricing concern, rep acknowledges with 'Okay, sounds good' but never circles back to confirm what was heard with a summary like 'So what I'm hearing is you want transparency on how pricing breaks down — did I get that right?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details: Gathered: property type (apartment), floor/stories (3rd floor origin, 2nd floor destination), unit numbers (832, 822), square footage (650-700 sq ft origin, destination not stated), truck parking (20 feet available, can park by entrance). Not gathered: number of rooms, walking distance, additional rooms beyond the four items (bed, mattress, sofa, desk), special considerations beyond what customer volunteered. Box count was explicitly rejected by customer ('no boxes'), so probing stopped there rather than exploring overflow.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Not offered. Rep does not ask the recognizable version ('Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'). Customer volunteers they are packing small/medium boxes themselves; rep does not offer packing as a service.
evidence_quotes.box_count: Not asked in the recognizable form. Customer volunteers 'I'll be doing most of the small boxes and medium boxes myself,' and rep responds 'So no boxes' — but the box-count/overflow-check question ('do you have anything like china or a book collection that might put you over a typical count?') is never asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives a range ('between two and a half to three and a half hours') and a personalized adjustment ('I definitely think you would fall within the two and a half hour range'), plus the dollar estimate ('$925 or $625'). However, the 'typical box count for a home this size' anchor is missing, since packing was not discussed and the customer rejected boxes. The estimate is narrowed to the customer's specific four items, which is personalization, but lacks the standard typical-range framing.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Fee transparency is present: 'trip fee of $75 from the second location back to the branch' is disclosed; hourly rate ($220) is disclosed; 'two and a half hour minimum,' 'pro rated in fifteen minute increments,' 'no hidden credit card fees,' and 'no deposit' are all stated. However, the 'not a guess' / commitment framing from the script is missing — rep does not frame the estimate as reliable or non-speculative in the way the rubric script calls for.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_silence: Not asked. Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or an equivalent. After the estimate and terms are laid out, rep pivots directly to the ask: 'Would you like us to help you on that move for Friday?' — no pause to gauge customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Partial. Rep states: 'we do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we mainly start discounting money of your final bill.' The discount concept is present, but the phrasing is vague ('mainly start discounting') and does not cover the terms clearly (how much, when does it start, etc.). Lacks the crisp framing of the recognizable version.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage: Full. Rep delivers: 'we do have our no worries damage coverage. Which is a free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate and that provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages and that's on top of the 60¢ per pound coverage that Texas requires us to have.' Coverage amount, no-fine-print framing ('included in the hourly rate'), and built-in status are all present.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after laying out the two promises. Instead, rep moves directly to the business ask. Additionally, the Two Promises section is delivered very early in the call (before the estimate and pricing discussion) and is not circled back to, so there is no proper loop closure.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. After the customer expresses price objection ('This seems to be a slightly, not slight actually be more than what I was expecting'), rep does not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or a genuine follow-up. Rep instead justifies the price ('We actually do not have any hi fees. Everything's included in our hourly rate') and the conversation ends with the customer declining.
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Not asked. Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' — the call ends immediately after the price objection and rep's justification.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Rep asks: 'Would you like us to help you on that move for Friday?' — plainly stated, no softened out offered at this moment. However, the ask comes too early (before the customer's price objection is fully resolved) and no follow-up ask is made after the objection is raised.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Not mentioned. Rep does not reference 'rate lock' or 'no-deposit' language. Rep does state 'there's no deposit to get on our schedule and there's actually no risk and securing your spot,' which touches on deposit but does not use the script's rate-lock framing.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. The customer declines with 'Yeah. This seems to be a slightly, not slight actually be more than what I was expecting. It's okay, I'll remove me, just end up calling friend or something.' Rep does not confirm any booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, notes). The call ends without a booking.

top_strength: Brianne delivered the No Worries Damage Coverage promise fully and clearly, including the $2,000 limit, no-deductible framing, and built-in status — this was the strongest single section delivery on the call.
coaching_note: Start every call with the quid pro quo (time-boxed ask + promise of a dependable quote) and wait for a yes before proceeding — this call skipped it entirely and set a weak foundation; additionally, when a customer raises a pricing concern, dig two layers deep into what's driving it rather than jumping to a defensive justification.
